stories.headline: Denver voters on track to approve all five city ballot measures, including foie gras ban
stories.summary:
Five Denver ballot measures were on track for victory Tuesday evening, each showing wide margins of support and polling at 65% or higher. They include Initiated Ordinance 311, a ban on the sale and production of foie gras in the city when force-feeding of animals is involved, along with four measures referred by the City Council.

As of 10 p.m., the foie gras ban had 66% support. Violators would face penalties of $1,000 to $5,000, and repeated violations could lead to a business license suspension of up to six months. Pro-Animal Colorado, the group that gathered signatures to put the measure on the ballot, declared victory at 7:40 p.m.

Question 2K, a new 20-year franchise agreement with Xcel Energy, was passing with about 69% support. Under the contract Denver would receive $32 million annually in franchise fees and $150 million in utility relocation benefits. The current agreement expires at the end of this year.

The other measures were also passing. Question 2H, adding wage enforcement to the Auditor's Office duties, had 86% support. Question 2I, allowing a two-year city budget process, had 65%. Question 2J, modernizing the Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety, had nearly 80%.

stories.headline: Early returns show Boebert trailing in 4th District as Kiros wins Denver seat
stories.summary:
Early unofficial results from Colorado's congressional races showed Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher with 50% of the vote to Republican U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert's 47% in the 4th Congressional District. Libertarian Douglas Mangeris had close to 3%. Boebert is seeking a fourth term in her second run in the 4th District after switching from the 3rd in 2024.

In the 1st Congressional District, Democrat Melat Kiros was declared the winner by the Associated Press about 20 minutes after initial results were posted. Kiros, 29, unseated 15-term U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette in the June primary and describes herself as a democratic socialist. She had 78% of early returns to Peterson's 14%.

In the 8th District, Democrat Manny Rutinel led Republican U.S. Rep. Gabe Evans 61% to 35% in early returns, with Libertarian Dave Wood at about 4%. The district, covering parts of Adams, Weld and Larimer counties, has been considered the state's most competitive House seat.

In the 3rd District, Republican U.S. Rep. Jeff Hurd and Democrat Dwayne Romero were locked in a tight race, with Romero at 49% to Hurd's 48% in the first results.

stories.headline: Front Range Passenger Rail sales tax poised to pass
stories.summary:
A measure creating a sales tax to fund the Front Range Passenger Rail District was poised to pass in Tuesday's election, according to CPR News. The measure authorizes a permanent 0.333 percent sales and use tax.

The tax is projected to generate $295 million a year and support $580 million in debt. The money would extend Colorado Connector service south of the already-funded Denver to Fort Collins starter segment.

The Denver Metro Chamber of Commerce and the El Paso County Board of County Commissioners opposed the new tax, as did the Independence Institute and Let's Go Colorado, among others.

stories.headline: Jury awards $200,000 to Mexican tourist bitten by Aurora police dog in 'fart police' case
stories.summary:
A Colorado jury on Tuesday awarded more than $200,000 to a Mexican tourist who was bitten by an Aurora police dog three years ago after officers gave nonsensical Spanish-language warnings. Jurors found dog handler Robert Wong liable for excessive force during a SWAT operation and officer Grant Peet liable for malicious prosecution. They did not find fault with officers Oscar Pena and Jeremiah Miles.

Salvador Alonso Guerrero-Salmeron was renting a room in an Aurora home on March 2, 2023, when officers arrived to arrest a different tenant. He alleged he was asleep and did not hear or understand commands announced in English and poorly pronounced Spanish. Officers repeatedly said, "Pedo policía pedo la madera," which a translator found meant "Fart police, fart the wood."

The dog bit the unarmed man on the arm for about 15 seconds as he held up his tourist visa and ID. Aurora attorneys argued officers acted reasonably because he did not comply for more than an hour. A municipal charge against him was later dropped.

His attorneys, Joshua Landy and Luke McConnell, said the verdict "sets the record straight" and noted the jury also imposed punitive damages for the malicious prosecution.

stories.headline: Colorado students to face shorter CMAS tests starting spring 2027
stories.summary:
The Colorado Department of Education is reducing the time students spend on state assessments beginning in spring 2027. Students in grades three through eight will have fewer Colorado Measures of Academic Success sessions, and those in grades five through eight will see math and science exams move from three sessions to two.

Testing time per subject will fall about 23% compared with 2026, without removing questions, reducing academic content or changing the information reported to families, the department said. The changes stem from a study required by House Bill 25-1278. Testing time in 2027 will be about two-thirds of what it was in 2015.

This year, 37.3% of students met or exceeded expectations in math and 44.8% in English. In Denver Public Schools, 42.5% met that mark in English and 32.9% in math, improving on last year but trailing state averages.

Boulder Valley, Jeffco, Cherry Creek, Littleton and Douglas County outpaced state averages, while Adams 12 Five Star and Aurora Public Schools trailed in both subjects.

stories.headline: Las Vegas developer plans 63-unit garage condo project near Centennial Airport
stories.summary:
Las Vegas-based Ventura Enterprises plans a 100,000-square-foot commercial condo development in Centennial, its first in Colorado. The 63-unit project offers spaces sized for car collectors and midsize businesses. Developer Leor Rozen, 30, bought the 7-acre site at 6507 S. Racine Circle this month for $3 million, nearly $10 per square foot.

The seller, Glenn McWilliams, who had previously entitled the site for a similar GarageCondos project, will consult on the development and is a part-owner and investor. Units will range from about 500 to 4,000 square feet and be listed between $150,000 and $1.3 million. Larger units have mezzanines and each has its own electrical meter.

Rozen said 30% of units have already sold. He said the company sought a new market because of rising land costs and limited development opportunity in Las Vegas, and calls the Centennial project My Dream Storage Co.

stories.headline: Nuggets fall to Trail Blazers 118-110 at home despite Murray's 35 points
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets lost to the Portland Trail Blazers 118-110 on Monday, dropping to 3-3 on the season and 1-2 at home. Portland out-rebounded Denver 53-37.

Denver also surrendered 36 fast-break points and gave up 41 three-pointers, with Portland shooting 36.6 percent from deep.

Jamal Murray scored 35 points on 10-of-19 shooting, going 4-of-9 from three and 11-of-11 at the free-throw line, adding six assists and five rebounds. He has scored 42, 39 and 35 points in his first six games.

stories.headline: Nuggets decline DaRon Holmes' 2027-28 team option
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets declined their rookie scale team option on forward DaRon Holmes worth $5.55 million for the 2027-28 season, according to league sources cited by HoopsHype's Michael Scotto.

Holmes was the 22nd pick of the 2024 NBA Draft. The decision means he is set to become a free agent after the 2026-27 season unless a new arrangement is reached.

stories.headline: Avalanche unveil 'Hometown Remix' uniforms
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche revealed new "Hometown Remix" uniforms as part of a league-wide release from the NHL and Fanatics. The design features a mountain elevation pattern in shades of blue on the front crest and numbers on the back, with Rocky Mountain details on the shoulder.

The blue and white jersey includes metallic silver on the sleeves and silver detailing around the logos, giving a frosted look. The NHL described it as evoking crisp mountain air and new snow.

Fanatics' Dom Fillion said the program involved collaboration with each club to reflect the history, culture and identity of every city and fan base.

topStory.headline: Democrats Win Control of Senate and House in Midterm Elections, Flipping Seats in Texas, Kansas and South Carolina
topStory.summary:
Democrats won control of the U.S. Senate and are expected to take the House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterm elections, according to The New York Times, The Guardian and NBC News. NBC News reported that Democrats will hold both chambers of Congress beginning in January after flipping seven Senate seats. According to the Associated Press, as cited by the Times, Democratic Senate pickups came in Maine, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, many of them in states that had long been Republican strongholds.

Several of the victories were historic. Democrat James Talarico defeated Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, whom President Trump had elevated to the Republican nomination, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Texas since 1988. In Kansas, the Rev. Adam Hamilton defeated Sen. Roger Marshall, the state's first Democratic Senate win since 1932, and in South Carolina, Dr. Annie Andrews won a seat for Democrats for the first time since 1998. In Maine, Sen. Susan Collins conceded to Troy Jackson, a former state legislator, and in Michigan, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed won despite a late endorsement of the Republican nominee by his defeated primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens. Counting continued in Alaska and in Mississippi, where a couple dozen votes separated the candidates, so Democrats could still widen their Senate margin.

Democrats also won significant governorships. Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected in Georgia and became the first Black woman elected governor in the country's history, and Gina Hinojosa ousted Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to become the first Democratic governor there since Ann Richards in 1990. Dr. Amy Acton became the first woman elected to lead Ohio, and Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford defeated Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo, according to NBC News projections. Republicans did win a notable race in Florida, where Byron Donalds was elected the state's first Black governor.

Trump said in an interview with The New York Times that he was "absolutely willing to accept those results" and would "look forward to working with" Democrats, adding, "We'll probably work something out." He also posted on social media, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" In an interview with Fox News, he pointed to his veto power, saying Democrats would "send over things that are insane and I'll veto them," and predicting that after "a couple of months of vetoes" the parties would work together. The Guardian reported that Trump held 30 campaign rallies over the past month and that, in remarks seen as aimed at voters unhappy with U.S. support for Israel, he said the United States would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after the end of this year.

The campaign was shaped by concerns over the cost of living, rising fuel prices and an unpopular war with Iran, and by record-low approval ratings for Trump, according to The Guardian. NBC News reported that Democrats regained ground in heavily Latino counties in Texas, where voters who shifted toward Trump in 2024 over economic concerns were also affected by federal immigration enforcement. Democratic control of Congress will give the party oversight powers and the ability to pass legislation, though Trump's veto authority will constrain what becomes law. Among Democrats, Rep. Ro Khanna called El-Sayed's win evidence that progressives can win nationally, a message that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has also promoted; both are considered potential 2028 presidential candidates but have not announced campaigns.
